symptom: `create or modify` of a flow whose `case` moved an enumeration value to another `when`, added one, took a `when` out or added one was refused: 'cannot replace the ExclusiveSplit … it has N paths, not two'. Every new enumeration value needs adding to every dispatcher on it (CE0079), and drop-and-create resets what Studio Pro drew.
cause: sameCaseShell compared the branch values, their count and their order as part of the shell, so any such change made the case unmatched and the diff fell back to replacing the whole split, which the splice only does for a two-path decision.
fix: The values and the branch list are no longer the shell: branches pair by a shared value (caseBranchPairs). A SetCaseValues edit, after the paired bodies are spliced, takes out a removed branch's path (plain activities only, as a decision drop), adds a new branch as a flow into the case merge with its body spliced and placed below the branches, re-points moved values' flows, and adds or takes out the merge in front of a multi-value branch.
insight: mxcli stores one flow per value (`when A, B` is two flows into a branch merge); the reader keeps only the first CaseValues entry, so putting several values on one flow is not an option. Measured: two value flows straight into an activity is CE0709 'Sequence flow is not accepted by origin or destination'; the merge is required, and a merge left with one incoming flow is the stray describe warns about (#923). A new branch's first value may already have a flow (a branch split back out): reuse it, or the value has two flows and the old one dangles. And compare annotations per side: describe prints per-value @anchor on a stored case the script never states, so a nil-vs-non-nil Annotations check silently unpaired the re-run.
test: mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice_case_values_2618_test.go (move, unchanged control, drop and refuse, take a branch out, add a branch); mdl/executor/cmd_flow_modify_case_values_2618_test.go fails with the old shell comparison. Live 11.12.6: the issue's repro (B joins A, B's when removed) and splitting it back out, a new two-value branch, each spliced in place with re-runs unchanged and mx check 0 errors; removing a branch that returns is refused.
